decisions.reason: Its premium hand-knotted wool-silk positioning matches the firm's craftsmanship and fine-material identity, and after two years of visible commitment management is inclined to justify the investment rather than reverse it.

Management still tends to persist with this publicly launched carpet, but as one of several similar low-pile rugs it remains a comparatively easy candidate for later range pruning if overlap becomes hard to defend.
The corner bench sits squarely in the firm's core furniture and project-interior business, so prior investment and strategic fit make continued support the more likely choice.

This carpet benefits from sunk development and marketing effort and will likely be kept, though carpets are less central than seating or casegoods and therefore somewhat easier to trim if resources are reallocated.
The swivel shell chair line involves broader investment across several models and aligns well with flexible workplace concepts, so escalation of commitment strongly favors continuation.
